title: [native_aot] bmm_outer_product: first Triton AOT op, block-size bucket dispatch
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.18.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #196508

Human Notes:

Use the new shiny triton AOT toolchain to embed an op.

Claude:

First op on the Triton toolchain: the shared triton.jit body lives in aot_kernel.py
(triton.tools.compile needs a bare kernel file), each spec point bakes one (dtype,
BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), and per-spec range guards dispatch M into block-size buckets.
The AOT signature has to match Triton's JIT specialization -- innermost strides
baked to 1, 16-byte alignment hints, i32 strides -- with the matching conditions in
both the prelude and coverage, or the AOT SASS is generically addressed and much
slower. The ABI narrows sizes and strides to int32_t, so both sides bound them too:
coverage wider than the stub's acceptance costs such a call its JIT route as well.

Four kernels (2 dtypes x 2 block sizes) cover every M, since the kernel masks the M
tail and takes M as a runtime i32, making the bucket edges a perf choice rather
than a correctness one. On an H100 BLOCK_M=32 (M <= 96) and 64 (above) are within
noise of _pick_block_sizes' per-M choices, worst case 0.94x at M=8, and all 32/32
measured shapes beat stock aten by 1.33x-3.93x; that measurement is why ARCHS names
Hopper explicitly instead of defaulting to every KNOWN_ARCHES.

Folded in is a pre-existing hole in the JIT cond, which accepted mixed dtypes:
aten's dtype-equality check lives in the meta function that neither layer runs, and
both specialize on self's dtype, so a bf16 mat2 was read through an f32 kernel and
returned garbage where aten raises. Both conds now require equal dtypes, the
prelude including out's. Separately, aot_kernel.py imports triton at module scope,
so it joins the DSL kernel modules the two import walks already exempt: CPU-only CI
has no triton.

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

Test Plan:

```
python test/python_native/test_native_aot_bmm.py
python test/python_native/test_instrumentation.py
python test/test_public_bindings.py TestPublicBindings.test_modules_can_be_imported
python test/test_testing.py TestImports.test_circular_dependencies
```

The import tests were run with triton masked, that being the configuration they
cover. End to end from a scratch build: 4 cubins exported for sm_90a and embedded
in libtorch_cuda, and with the JIT layer off every M from 1 to 4096 routes to
_bmm_outer_product_aot_kernel with results bitwise equal to `a @ b`.

items.author: albanD
items.body:
I think this one from claude is real:
In the case whre you have triton but a PT build without stage 2:
  1. The router is installed.
  2. covers_bmm doesn't exist, so the Python covered_axes runs.
  3. It returns True for an fp32/bf16 outer product with N >= 128.
  4. The router returns _NO_MATCH, and plain aten runs.

So we will always skip the jit impl even when using a non-AOT-enabled build

  This hasn't happened before because the only other declaration, topk, gates on device capability in its
  own covered_axes. That hides the fact that the infra lets a declaration with no shipped kernels still
  decline calls.

  That points to two possible fixes:
  - In this PR: add an arch and ROCm gate to bmm's covered_axes, matching topk.
  - In the infra: have covers() return False when the op's covers_<op> isn't registered, or when
    _native_aot_embedded() is False. This is in aot_manifest.py, which this PR doesn't touch; it may
    belong in the base PR (#196507) or a follow-up. It's the more robust option, since it protects every
    future declaration.

@@ -0,0 +1,160 @@
+"""Native-AOT declaration for aten::bmm @ CUDA (outer-product, K == 1), the first
+triton-kind op. A point is (dtype, BLOCK_M) plus the M range it serves; fp16, N < 128 and
+non-CUDA stay with the JIT override."""
+
+ATEN_OP = "bmm"
+DISPATCH_KEY = "CUDA"
+KERNEL_MODULE = "aot_kernel.py"
+# Stated, or the default claims every KNOWN_ARCHES. Both spellings, since either can
+# appear in TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST and export matches them exactly.
+ARCHS = ("sm_90", "sm_90a", "sm_100", "sm_100a")
+
+_DTYPES = {"float32": "at::kFloat", "bfloat16": "at::kBFloat16"}
+# (BLOCK_M, m_lo, m_hi], m_hi None being unbounded: the kernel masks the M tail, so the
+# edges are a perf choice, measured within noise of _pick_block_sizes' on an H100. Two
+# points rather than one per M: a fixed BLOCK_M=64 halves occupancy at small M. The
+# worst measured case is M=8 at 0.94x of the JIT's next_power_of_2 choice, taken over
+# more points because coverage moves these calls off the JIT route entirely, so an
+# extra bucket edge buys nothing a compile does not cost back.
+_M_BUCKETS = [(32, 0, 96), (64, 96, None)]
+_MIN_N = 128
+_INT32_MAX = 2**31 - 1
+
+
+def kernel_precompile_grid():
+    # "outer" must appear, or a non-outer call would match on dtype alone.
+    return [
+        {
+            "dtype": list(_DTYPES),
+            "outer": True,
+            "BLOCK_M": bm,
+            "BLOCK_N": 128,
+            "m_lo": lo,
+            "m_hi": hi,
+        }
+        for bm, lo, hi [truncated]

+# Owner(s): ["module: dsl-native-ops"]
+"""End-to-end tests for the native-AOT bmm outer-product kernels @ CUDA.
+
+Compared exactly: K == 1 is a per-element product, with no accumulation order to differ
+from the reference. Tests needing the AOT library skip without it."""
+
+import contextlib
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+from torch.testing._internal.common_cuda import TEST_CUDA
+from torch.testing._internal.common_utils import (
+    instantiate_parametrized_tests,
+    parametrize,
+    run_tests,
+    skipIfNoNativeAot,
+    skipIfNoTritonDSL,
+    TestCase,
+)
+
+
+def _ran_aot(fn) -> bool:
+    # Both layers launch the same-named kernel, so attribution needs the JIT side
+    # masked rather than a profiler name match.
+    from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity
+
+    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
+        fn()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return any(
+        "_bmm_outer_product_aot_kernel" in e.name
+        for e in prof.events()
+        if e.device_type.name == "CUDA"
+    )
+
+
+def _load_covered_axes():
+    # By path, through the loader the declaration tooling itself uses: aot.py is
+    # stdlib-only at import, and nothing imports it as a module.
+    import os
+
+    from torchgen.native_aot_decl import load_by_path
+
+    path = os.path.join(
+        os.path.dirname(torch.__file__), "_native", "ops", "bmm_outer_product", "aot.py"
+    )
+    return load_by_path("bmm_outer_product_ao [truncated]
